ENTJ>INTJ.title: Even after deciding, you go over it again at home.
ENTJ>INTJ.body: In front of people, you can decide quickly and keep things moving. But you firm up your thinking in quiet time alone. Thinking ahead, deciding with logic, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality.
ENTJ>INTJ.say: "This is the overall plan. I'll send the details by tomorrow."
ENTJ>INTJ.do: When you're given a task, you count back from the deadline and decide what to do on which day.
ENTJ>INTJ.worry: The more you lead people, the less time you have to think alone. You're glad to be relied on, but some days you want quiet, and balancing the two wears you out.
ENTJ>INTJ.karai: When you're put in charge of a trip, you send everyone a table that even has travel times.
ENTJ>INTJ.aru: In the meeting you can say, "We're going with this," but at home you're going over the same plan until midnight.
ENTJ>INTJ.why: Thinking ahead, deciding with logic, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. What's different is where your energy comes from. Your temperament gets energy from being with people, and your personality grew toward firming up ideas alone. That's why you want both time with people and time to think alone.
ENTJ>INTJ.yure: The question that makes you waver is "Do people give you energy, or do you need time alone?" It depends on whether you picture yourself running a meeting or fixing documents at night.
ENTJ>INTJ.plus: You can make decisions in front of people and finish things on your own, so your team can really count on you. Wanting time to think isn't selfish.
ENTJ>INTJ.tip: When you make plans to see people, keep the next evening free. If your time alone is already set, you can enjoy the day with people too.
ENTJ>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to sort out your thoughts by talking with people. Have you ever been explaining a stuck plan to someone and suddenly seen the answer? Talk to people earlier, and your work moves faster.

ENTJ>INTP.title: After deciding, you ask yourself, "Really?"
ENTJ>INTP.body: You decide fast, then right away start thinking, "But is that really right?" Trusting ideas and checking them with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. You can decide quickly, and you can think things through slowly too.
ENTJ>INTP.say: "It's decided, but let me hear one other option first."
ENTJ>INTP.do: With big news stories, you read a few articles to check if they're true.
ENTJ>INTP.worry: Even when you want to decide quickly, the more you think, the more other answers you see, and you get stuck. You want days leading people and days thinking alone, so packing your schedule wears you out.
ENTJ>INTP.karai: Before buying an appliance, you check several comparison sites, then go to the store.
ENTJ>INTP.aru: Five minutes after saying, "OK, that's decided," you flip it yourself: "Actually, maybe not."
ENTJ>INTP.why: Your temperament moves with people and pushes forward once it decides. Your personality grew toward thinking slowly alone and keeping things open. That's why quick decisions and second thoughts take turns. Ideas and logic are the same in both, so your way of thinking stays steady.
ENTJ>INTP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on "Do people give you energy?" and "Plan ahead or go with the moment?" The result depends on whether you answer as the you leading people or the you looking things up.
ENTJ>INTP.plus: You rethink even after deciding because you're really looking for a better answer. You can decide fast and think deeply, all on your own.
ENTJ>INTP.tip: Once you decide, tell people first: "I won't change this for a week." Saying it out loud makes it harder to flip, and you can save the rethinking for next time.
ENTJ>INTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to gather people and get things moving fast. It shows when a discussion stalls and you can't help saying, "OK, let's do this." Use it, and your ideas turn into reality faster.

ENTJ>ENTJ.title: Once the goal is set, the steps come to you right away.
ENTJ>ENTJ.body: Once a goal is set, the steps line up in your head right away. Moving with people, thinking ahead, deciding with logic, and following a plan are exactly the same in your temperament and personality. That's why you always end up as the organizer. In places where nothing gets decided, you get tired easily.
ENTJ>ENTJ.say: "So what do you want in the end?"
ENTJ>ENTJ.do: Even on days off you decide, "Shopping in the morning, gym in the afternoon," and feel good when it goes that way.
ENTJ>ENTJ.worry: You move at your own pace and only later notice others haven't kept up. You want even rest to have a purpose, so it's hard to relax.
ENTJ>ENTJ.karai: Even on a day you said you'd take it easy, you've finished three errands by noon.
ENTJ>ENTJ.aru: When a trip comes up with friends, you're the one deciding where to go and when to meet. When everyone's unsure, you can't help saying, "OK, let's do this."
ENTJ>ENTJ.why: Both your temperament and personality lean toward moving with people, thinking ahead, deciding with logic, and following a plan. All four match, so this strength has grown very solid. That's why you naturally decide how to move forward when everyone else is unsure.
ENTJ>ENTJ.yure: You're likely to get nearly the same result every time you take the test. If a different one shows up, you may have been worn out and low on social energy, or going through a stretch of matching other people's pace.
ENTJ>ENTJ.plus: You decide first because you don't want to waste anyone's time. Trips always go smoothly because you got things ready ahead of time.
ENTJ>ENTJ.tip: On trips, let your friends choose just the dinner spot. You'll end up somewhere you wouldn't pick, and that's one more thing to enjoy.
ENTJ>ENTJ.hidden: You're great at sticking to plans, and you can also enjoy the unplanned. Have you ever had plans rained out, just hung around at home, and found it surprisingly fun? Use it, and people around you will feel more relaxed with you.

ENTJ>ENTP.title: You keep changing how you do things, right on the spot.
ENTJ>ENTP.body: You always meet the deadline. But you think how you get there can change with your mood that day. Getting energy from people, trusting ideas, and thinking with logic are the same in your temperament and personality.
ENTJ>ENTP.say: "As long as it's done by Friday, do it however you like."
ENTJ>ENTP.do: When you think of a new way, you immediately ask everyone, "Want to try it?"
ENTJ>ENTP.worry: You want to stick to what you decided, and you want to try more interesting ways, both at once. When you keep changing how things are done, you worry you're jerking people around.
ENTJ>ENTP.karai: While helping a friend with a problem, you get more fired up than they are.
ENTJ>ENTP.aru: You planned the order of places for the trip, but when you arrive you think, "Actually, I'm curious about that shop," and change the plan yourself.
ENTJ>ENTP.why: Getting energy from people, trusting ideas, and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. The only difference is how you move forward. Your temperament likes to plan and follow through, and your personality grew toward adapting on the spot. That's why you can enjoy both the plan and the detours.
ENTJ>ENTP.yure: The question that makes you waver is "Do you plan ahead or decide on the spot?" Picture a work deadline, and you lean toward planning. Picture a day off, and you lean toward the spot.
ENTJ>ENTP.plus: You want to change plans because you notice more interesting ways. Someone who keeps the goal and changes the method is a big help when things keep changing.
ENTJ>ENTP.tip: When you go out with friends, say at the start, "Let's decide the afternoon when we get there." Then changing plans is part of the deal, and no one feels jerked around.
ENTJ>ENTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to work back from the goal and set the order. It shows when a deadline gets close and your head suddenly clears and you start lining up tasks. Use it earlier, and people at work will trust you as someone who always finishes.

ENTJ>INFJ.title: You think about whether everyone can keep it up without strain.
ENTJ>INFJ.body: When a junior talks about their future, you're already thinking about their plan in your head. Picturing what's ahead and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. You can decide with logic and notice how people feel, so you see the ones who might get left behind.
ENTJ>INFJ.say: "With this goal, I think everyone can keep going without pushing too hard."
ENTJ>INFJ.do: After a drama ends, you keep thinking about why the characters did what they did.
ENTJ>INFJ.worry: Even when you know the right direction, you can't say it if someone might get hurt. On days you've thought too much about others' feelings, you only feel like yourself again after time alone.
ENTJ>INFJ.karai: You say "Let's think about it later," but by bedtime you've already decided.
ENTJ>INFJ.aru: In the meeting you can quickly say, "Let's go this way," but the face of the person who barely spoke stays on your mind all the way home.
ENTJ>INFJ.why: Picturing what's ahead and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament leads in front of people and decides with logic. Your personality grew toward quietly sensing how people feel. You have both the power to decide and the power to notice, so your heart gets busy.
ENTJ>INFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself deciding as a leader or helping a friend with a problem.
ENTJ>INFJ.plus: You quickly notice people who might get left behind because you really look at each person. When someone moves the team forward without leaving anyone behind, the whole mood changes.
ENTJ>INFJ.tip: If someone's on your mind, ask everyone once at the end of the meeting: "Anyone else have thoughts?" You'll hear from them right there, so it won't follow you home as much.
ENTJ>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to step up in front of people and move things along. It shows when a friend is stuck and you find yourself calling the shop for them and sorting it out. Use it, and you can show your kindness through action.

ENTJ>INFP.title: When you want to do something, you go all in.
ENTJ>INFP.body: When you say, "We have to do this project," your eyes are already looking a little ahead. Being drawn to possibilities that don't have a shape yet is you, from every angle. You have both the drive to rally people and get results and the need to think things over alone; the push to decide and move, and the softness to take a detour your heart asks for.
ENTJ>INFP.say: "If I'm doing it, I want to do something I really believe in."
ENTJ>INFP.do: When you think of something you want to do, you picture it going well again and again.
ENTJ>INFP.worry: Wanting results and wanting it to feel right rarely point the same way. After a day of leading people, you need more alone time than you expect.
ENTJ>INFP.karai: Watching the news, you start wondering, "What'll it be like in ten years?"
ENTJ>INFP.aru: You got everyone excited with "Let's do this!", then on the way home you wonder, "Is this really what I want?"
ENTJ>INFP.why: Only one thing matches in your temperament and character: your heart turns toward possibilities that don't exist yet. The other three point different ways. A born strength for leading, deciding by logic, and following plans sits alongside a character that thinks feelings over alone, decides by heart, and moves with its mood. You go back and forth because both are truly yours.
ENTJ>INFP.yure: Three of your four tendencies differ, so your result can change a lot from test to test. Answer as the person out doing things with friends, or as the one listening to music alone at night, and you may get a completely different type.
ENTJ>INFP.plus: You stop to think because you want to stay honest with yourself. When your drive to lead is backed by real conviction, you won't second-guess the road you chose.
ENTJ>INFP.tip: Before starting something new, tell a friend you trust why you want to do it. Saying it out loud makes your reason clear, so it's easier to remember when you start to doubt.
ENTJ>INFP.hidden: You tend to follow your mood and feelings, but there's also a strength in you that sees things through to the end. Right before a move or a trip, you suddenly set the order and knock tasks out one by one. That's it. Use it on what you love, and your ideas won't stay just dreams.

ENTJ>ENFJ.title: You keep things moving while checking in on everyone.
ENTJ>ENFJ.body: You can state the team's goal clearly. You also notice right away when someone's voice gets a little quieter. Getting energy from people, looking ahead, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality.
ENTJ>ENFJ.say: "This is our goal for the month. Let's do it together!"
ENTJ>ENFJ.do: After a meeting, you ask someone who seems down, "You OK?"
ENTJ>ENFJ.worry: When you should be firm, you picture their face and end up too soft. Trying to move everyone forward, you're the one running around the most.
ENTJ>ENFJ.karai: When "When should we meet?" stalls in the group chat, you quickly drop three possible dates.
ENTJ>ENFJ.aru: You'd decided to talk to a junior about a mistake, but when you see their face, you end up softening how you say it.
ENTJ>ENFJ.why: Getting energy from people, looking ahead, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. The only difference is how you decide. Your temperament decides with logic, and your personality grew toward caring about people's feelings. You get stuck between firm and kind because you can do both.
ENTJ>ENFJ.yure: The key question is "Logic or feelings?" Picture work where you deliver numbers, and you lean toward logic. Picture looking after a junior, and you lean toward feelings.
ENTJ>ENFJ.plus: You soften your words because you really think about how the other person feels. People naturally follow a leader who gets results and still takes care of people.
ENTJ>ENFJ.tip: When you correct someone, pair "this is what happened" with "next time, please do this." It won't sound like blame, and they'll know right away what to fix.
ENTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to separate feelings from facts. It shows when a friend asks for love advice and you're the calmest one saying, "That's on them, not you." Use it, and you'll be more than kind; you'll really help people move forward.

ENTJ>ENFP.title: You actually make your fun ideas happen.
ENTJ>ENFP.body: A surprise you started on a whim somehow ends with you planning the whole day and the budget. Getting energy from people and liking to imagine new things are the same in your temperament and personality. You can turn fun ideas into something real.
ENTJ>ENFP.say: "Anyone want to go to next month's festival? I'll get the tickets."
ENTJ>ENFP.do: Even with someone you just met, you quickly get excited talking about things you both love.
ENTJ>ENFP.worry: You want to keep starting fun things, but you also want to finish everything you start, so you get busy. With someone who just wants you to listen, you jump to the practical stuff first and regret it later.
ENTJ>ENFP.karai: The longest message in the group chat is usually from you.
ENTJ>ENFP.aru: You're the one who said, "Let's keep it casual," but somehow you're the most serious about setting times and roles.
ENTJ>ENFP.why: Getting energy from people and trusting ideas are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament decides with logic and follows through. Your personality grew toward valuing feelings and acting in the moment. That's why having fun and running things always come together for you.
ENTJ>ENFP.yure: You tend to waver on "logic or feelings" and "plan or go with the moment." Your answers change depending on whether you picture yourself preparing an event or hanging out with friends.
ENTJ>ENFP.plus: You end up running things because you really want to make everyone's fun happen. Not many people can take an idea and actually do it.
ENTJ>ENFP.tip: At the next get-together, hand one whole job over to someone else. With less to run, you'll get to enjoy it too.
ENTJ>ENFP.hidden: When a friend is venting, do you ever find yourself thinking, "Maybe this is the cause"? That's your temperament's power to find causes with logic. Use it along with your kind listening, and people will rely on you even more for advice.

ENTJ>ISTJ.title: Even with big goals, you check the numbers first.
ENTJ>ISTJ.body: Right after you announce a big goal, you start checking last month's data. Deciding with logic and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. You can turn what you want to do into a real plan with numbers and steps.
ENTJ>ISTJ.say: "First, can I see last month's numbers?"
ENTJ>ISTJ.do: Before shopping, you decide what to buy and how much to spend, and you don't go over.
ENTJ>ISTJ.worry: Between wanting to try something new and wanting a sure method, it takes you a while to decide. When you're the organizer for too long, you start missing quiet time to work.
ENTJ>ISTJ.karai: You arrive 10 minutes early and think the friend who shows up right on time is "late."
ENTJ>ISTJ.aru: The same night you think, "It'd be fun to open a shop like this," you're looking up rent on your phone and doing the math.
ENTJ>ISTJ.why: Deciding with logic and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament pulls people in and thinks about what's ahead. Your personality grew toward checking facts alone and building step by step. That's why dreaming big and checking details can happen on the same day.
ENTJ>ISTJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Facts or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself pitching a new project or comparing data.
ENTJ>ISTJ.plus: Even if it takes time to get started, you're less likely to fail. You can turn big things into something truly doable with numbers and steps.
ENTJ>ISTJ.tip: Decide to start once you understand about 70 percent. The other 30 percent you can only learn by doing, so this keeps you from researching forever.
ENTJ>ISTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to get people involved and move things forward. It shows when, as soon as you're ready, you start calling everyone involved and end up as the organizer. Use it, and you can make your solid plans even bigger.

ENTJ>ISFJ.title: You quickly notice when people around you need help.
ENTJ>ISFJ.body: You see things through once you've decided. You can stand in front of people, and you can support them from behind. What's the same in your temperament and personality is following a plan. You often notice the small troubles of people around you.
ENTJ>ISFJ.say: "Are you feeling okay? Let's not push it — a little at a time."
ENTJ>ISFJ.do: Helping a friend move, you decide the order to carry things and tell everyone.
ENTJ>ISFJ.worry: Even when you want to take the lead, you step back out of care for others. The harder you try to do your part well, the more your own rest gets pushed back.
ENTJ>ISFJ.karai: You finished packing for the trip three days ago, so the night before there's nothing left to do.
ENTJ>ISFJ.aru: While making the team's plan for the year, you also put everyone's birthday on the calendar.
ENTJ>ISFJ.why: Following a plan is the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament stands in front of people, looks ahead, and decides with logic. Your personality grew toward quietly supporting the people in front of you and caring about feelings. That's why you can see both the big picture and the small troubles of people close to you.
ENTJ>ISFJ.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as the you setting direction at work, or the you looking after family and friends, and you may get totally different types.
ENTJ>ISFJ.plus: You remember birthdays because you care about each person. Not many people keep an eye on the future and on the people close to them.
ENTJ>ISFJ.tip: Leave birthdays and anniversaries to your phone's reminders, and don't try so hard to remember everything. That frees you up to focus on bigger plans.
ENTJ>ISFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to picture years ahead. It shows when you listen to a junior and think, "In three years, they'll be a leader." Tell them, and it becomes a way to help people grow.

ENTJ>ESTJ.title: You make the way things work at your job a little better, step by step.
ENTJ>ESTJ.body: When you pitch a new project, you bring three examples of past successes. Getting energy from people, deciding with logic, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. You can think up new things and also value the ways that already work.
ENTJ>ESTJ.say: "Okay, tomorrow we start with this one."
ENTJ>ESTJ.do: When a number at work bugs you, you go check it yourself before asking anyone.
ENTJ>ESTJ.worry: You want to change things, and you also want to protect what's working, so you're unsure how far to go. You tend to use yourself as the standard and expect others to move at your speed.
ENTJ>ESTJ.karai: Right after saying, "Do it however you like," you explain exactly how to do it.
ENTJ>ESTJ.aru: While talking about wanting to buy a house someday, you're also keeping close track of how much this month's electric bill went up.
ENTJ>ESTJ.why: Getting energy from people, deciding with logic, and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. What's different is how you see things. Your temperament pictures what's ahead, and your personality grew toward valuing experience and facts. That's why wanting to change things and wanting to protect them show up at the same time.
ENTJ>ESTJ.yure: Questions about how you see things are where your answers split. Picture yourself planning a new project, and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself running daily work, and you lean toward facts.
ENTJ>ESTJ.plus: Even when you think up new things, you're paying attention to what's really happening on the ground. That's why people feel safe following your decisions.
ENTJ>ESTJ.tip: When you suggest something new, say first, "Only this part changes; everything else stays the same." When people know what isn't changing, they'll listen with less worry.
ENTJ>ESTJ.hidden: While doing your usual work, do you ever think, "This could work for something else too"? That's your temperament's power to find what no one has noticed yet. When it happens, tell someone nearby right away, and it could start a new project.

ENTJ>ESFJ.title: You go around thanking everyone.
ENTJ>ESFJ.body: You prepare for events carefully, and on the day you go around thanking everyone. Getting energy from people and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. You care about results and about everyone having a good time.
ENTJ>ESFJ.say: "Let's hear everyone out and decide today."
ENTJ>ESFJ.do: When meeting friends, you set the time to wrap up around everyone's trains home.
ENTJ>ESFJ.worry: Even when you want results, you don't want to upset anyone. You're so glad to be relied on that you take on too much, and suddenly your schedule is full.
ENTJ>ESFJ.karai: You plan everyone's seats and put yourself at the end, where it's easy to order.
ENTJ>ESFJ.aru: You prepared the event perfectly, but on the day you're so busy checking that everyone's having fun that you barely eat.
ENTJ>ESFJ.why: Getting energy from people and following a plan are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament pictures what's ahead and decides with logic. Your personality grew toward watching the people in front of you and caring about their feelings. That's why you can handle the planning and the caring at the same time.
ENTJ>ESFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "logic or feelings." The result depends on whether you answer as the you setting direction in a meeting or the you planning a welcome party.
ENTJ>ESFJ.plus: You care more about others than yourself because you really want everyone to enjoy themselves. Get-togethers with you there always feel good.
ENTJ>ESFJ.tip: On event days, decide that you'll sit and eat for the first 15 minutes. Everyone's busy eating at the start anyway, so looking after people can wait a bit.
ENTJ>ESFJ.hidden: When a discussion drags on and you can smoothly say, "OK, let's decide this much today," that's your temperament's power to decide quickly with logic. Use it along with your thoughtfulness, and you can take care of everyone's time and feelings.

ENTJ>ISTP.title: You get it done with your hands before you talk about it.
ENTJ>ISTP.body: People may see you as someone who doesn't say much but delivers results first. Thinking with logic and deciding that way is the same in your temperament and personality. You can set goals, and you can get things done with your own hands.
ENTJ>ISTP.do: Once something's decided, you keep the explanation short and start your own work right away.
ENTJ>ISTP.worry: Sometimes you want to plan far ahead, sometimes you want to act on the spot, and the switching makes it hard to find your own pace. When you're put in charge, you start wanting time to work alone with your hands.
ENTJ>ISTP.karai: Your face says it'd be faster to just fix it quietly than to talk about it in a meeting.
ENTJ>ISTP.aru: When an appliance acts up, you start poking at it to fix it before reading the manual, and your family says, "Talk to us first."
ENTJ>ISTP.why: Deciding with logic is the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament leads people, thinks ahead, and follows a plan. Your personality grew toward working alone with your hands, looking at the facts in front of you, and figuring things out on the spot. The power to set goals and the power to quietly get to work are both yours.
ENTJ>ISTP.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Depending on whether you picture yourself talking about goals as a leader or working alone, your type can change quite a bit.
ENTJ>ISTP.plus: Your hands move before you explain because you need to check things for real. You can set the goal and finish it yourself, so your plans never stay just talk.
ENTJ>ISTP.tip: Before you start working on something, just say, "I'm going to do this now." It cuts down a lot on mix-ups with your family or team.
ENTJ>ISTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to organize people and plan ahead. It shows when, on a trip with friends, you find yourself sorting out the transfers and the budget. Use it at work, and you'll go from "skilled" to "someone we can leave it to."

ENTJ>ISFP.title: When it matters, you decide firmly.
ENTJ>ISFP.body: Usually you're smiling and listening. But when it matters, you decide so firmly that people are surprised. Your temperament and personality are opposite on all four sides, so you can seem quite different depending on the situation.
ENTJ>ISFP.say: "I really like this. I could look at it forever."
ENTJ>ISFP.do: For things in your room, you choose by whether they make you feel good, not by price.
ENTJ>ISFP.worry: You want things calm, but when things drag on, you're secretly annoyed. You hold in what you want to say, and later it can come out suddenly and too strongly.
ENTJ>ISFP.karai: On a day off you said you'd do nothing, you start rearranging your room.
ENTJ>ISFP.aru: You say, "Anywhere's fine," when picking a café, but you end up leading everyone to a quiet place with outlets.
ENTJ>ISFP.why: All four sides are different in this combination. Your temperament leads people, thinks ahead, decides with logic, and follows a plan. Your personality grew toward valuing time alone, what you sense in the moment, and people's feelings, and acting on the spot. That's why there's a firm side inside your gentle one.
ENTJ>ISFP.yure: All four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as the you carrying responsibility at work, or the you on a day off surrounded by things you love, and you may get opposite types.
ENTJ>ISFP.plus: Even though you're gentle, there are things you won't give up. That means you know clearly what matters to you.
ENTJ>ISFP.tip: When you do have a preference, add one line: "Anywhere's fine, but somewhere quiet would be nice." That alone makes it easier for others to choose.
ENTJ>ISFP.hidden: When you go shopping with a friend, do you ever casually say, "This one will last longer"? That's your temperament's power to judge things with logic. Use it when you're going along with others, and your words will carry more weight.

ENTJ>ESTP.title: When it counts, you decide in a flash.
ENTJ>ESTP.body: You plan carefully, but once you're in the moment, your body moves before you think. Getting energy from people and deciding fast with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. That's why you're strong when it really counts.
ENTJ>ESTP.say: "We can talk later! Let's grab the seats first."
ENTJ>ESTP.do: When a friend can't decide what to buy, you're quick to say, "This one's the better deal."
ENTJ>ESTP.worry: Even when you want to plan ahead, you jump at whatever's fun in front of you, and the plan gets pushed back. You skip checks to move fast, and sometimes regret it later.
ENTJ>ESTP.karai: When a friend vents, you say "OK, here's what to do" before "I get it."
ENTJ>ESTP.aru: You prepared your presentation carefully, but when you see their faces, you change the order right on the spot.
ENTJ>ESTP.why: Getting energy from people and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament looks ahead and makes plans. Your personality grew toward reading what's in front of you and acting on the spot. That's why you can prepare and still change your approach in the moment.
ENTJ>ESTP.yure: You tend to waver on "facts or ideas" and "plan or the moment." The result depends on whether you answer as the you taking time to prepare or the you deciding quickly on site.
ENTJ>ESTP.plus: You can change your approach on the spot because you watch people's reactions closely. Someone who can prepare and also adapt in the moment is strong.
ENTJ>ESTP.tip: When you prepare, pick one thing you'll make sure to say. Keep that one thing, and you can change the rest on the spot without losing your point.
ENTJ>ESTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to read where things are heading years ahead. It shows when you see the news and just know, "This is going to be big next year." Trust that hunch and move a little early, and you can stay a step ahead at work too.

ENTJ>ESFP.title: You get everyone excited and lead them right along.
ENTJ>ESFP.body: At the after-party, you're the one getting everyone hyped, and you quietly start talking about the next goal. Getting more energy the more you're with people is the same in your temperament and personality. You can move everyone forward while keeping the mood fun.
ENTJ>ESFP.do: At parties, you talk to people who are new so they can join the conversation.
ENTJ>ESFP.worry: Even when you want to enjoy the moment, part of your mind is always on the next thing to prepare. Because you care about everyone's feelings, you tend to dwell on it after saying something tough.
ENTJ>ESFP.karai: With an empty weekend coming, by Friday night you've texted someone, "Free tomorrow?"
ENTJ>ESFP.aru: It was a trip you decided on a whim, but somehow you're the one carefully booking the hotel and the train times.
ENTJ>ESFP.why: Getting energy from people is the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament thinks ahead, decides with logic, and follows a plan. Your personality grew toward valuing fun in the moment and people's feelings, and acting on the spot. That's why you can liven things up and pull everything together too.
ENTJ>ESFP.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as the person in charge of a team, or as the you having fun with friends, and you may get completely different types.
ENTJ>ESFP.plus: Not many people can take something decided on a whim and see it through. You can get people excited and pull things together, so you're counted on wherever you go.
ENTJ>ESFP.tip: Don't carry all the prep alone; split jobs like "hype person" and "cleanup" with someone. That way you get time to enjoy yourself too.
ENTJ>ESFP.hidden: While listening to a friend, do ideas pop up like, "That could be even more fun if..."? That's your temperament's power to picture what's ahead. Use it at work too, and you'll go from the fun one to the one trusted with planning.

ENTP>INTJ.title: You think your ideas through, on your own.
ENTP>INTJ.body: You take ideas that come up while chatting and think them through alone until they become a plan. Getting excited about what's ahead and thinking with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. You can spread ideas out, and you can finish them too.
ENTP>INTJ.say: "Wouldn't it be interesting to think about it backwards?"
ENTP>INTJ.do: When you see a new product everyone's talking about, you look up how it works before buying.
ENTP>INTJ.worry: Even when you want to build ideas by talking, too much talking tires you out and you want to be alone. Between wanting to try right away and wanting to plan first, you often start late.
ENTP>INTJ.karai: You pick up one book at a bookstore, and that night you stay up late watching related videos.
ENTP>INTJ.aru: The next day, you're explaining how to actually do something you thought up while chatting with a friend. Your friend says, "Wait, you were serious?"
ENTP>INTJ.why: Trusting ideas and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament builds ideas by talking with people and acts on the spot. Your personality grew toward thinking alone and planning far ahead. That's why you can both spread ideas out and finish them.
ENTP>INTJ.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Planner or go-with-the-moment?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself tossing out ideas while chatting or looking things up alone.
ENTP>INTJ.plus: You can turn ideas into something real fast because you can see how to do it in your head. Not many people can take an idea all the way to the finish.
ENTP>INTJ.tip: When you have an idea, tell just one person, "I'm thinking about this," before you work it out in detail. You'll get feedback early, and it'll turn out even better.
ENTP>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to build ideas while talking with people. It shows when a casual chat turns into an exciting new plan with someone. Share your thoughts early, and your ideas will grow even more.

ENTP>INTP.title: You love talking, and you love thinking alone.
ENTP>INTP.body: One minute you're leaning in, saying, "Tell me more!", and the next you suddenly want to think alone. Trusting ideas, thinking with logic, and going with the moment are the same in your temperament and personality. What's different is where your energy comes from.
ENTP>INTP.say: "Give me a sec to think about this on my own."
ENTP>INTP.do: When something catches your interest, you spend your whole day off looking into it.
ENTP>INTP.worry: There's a big gap between days you want to talk and days you don't want to see anyone, so planning is hard. Thinking is so fun that sometimes you feel satisfied before actually doing anything.
ENTP>INTP.karai: On days with no one to talk to, you argue with online articles in your head.
ENTP>INTP.aru: When a conversation with friends gets going, you're the most into it, but the moment you get home, you don't want to talk to anyone.
ENTP>INTP.why: Ideas, logic, and going with the moment are the same in your temperament and personality. The only difference is where your energy comes from. Your temperament gets energy from talking with people, and your personality grew toward recharging by thinking alone. The gap between social days and alone days is big because you have two ways to recharge.
ENTP>INTP.yure: Your answers split on "Do people give you energy, or do you need time alone?" Depending on whether you picture a night of deep talk with friends or time alone at home looking things up, you may go back and forth between two types.
ENTP>INTP.plus: You go quiet at home because you're thinking over what you talked about. That's why your thoughts go deep.
ENTP>INTP.tip: On weekends, make plans for only one of the two days. Knowing you can rest the next day lets you enjoy the day you're invited out all the way through.
ENTP>INTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to quickly warm up to people you've just met. It shows when, at a gathering full of strangers, you find yourself asking questions and keeping the conversation going. Use it, and you'll make more new connections at work too.

ENTP>ENTJ.title: When you get an idea, you set the plan that same day.
ENTP>ENTJ.body: You pitch a fun idea in a meeting, and before you know it you've already set who does what and by when. Getting energy from people and checking ideas with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. You can come up with ideas and pull them together, all by yourself.
ENTP>ENTJ.say: "How about this? Let's try it once by next week."
ENTP>ENTJ.do: You started working out on a whim, but by week two you're tracking reps and weight in an app.
ENTP>ENTJ.worry: Wanting to try new ideas clashes with wanting to stick to the plan, and sometimes you get trapped by your own rules. You move so fast that you're slow to notice people who can't keep up.
ENTP>ENTJ.karai: The hobby you "just sort of started" has somehow become the most serious one.
ENTP>ENTJ.aru: You just said, "Let's take a trip!" on a whim, and the next day you've set the dates and budget and posted them in the group chat.
ENTP>ENTJ.why: Getting energy from people, trusting ideas, and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and personality. What's different is how you move forward. Your temperament likes to go with the flow, and your personality grew toward looking ahead and following through. That's why your ideas turn into plans so fast.
ENTP>ENTJ.yure: Your answers wobble on "Do you like to plan or go with the moment?" Picture yourself running a project at work, and you lean toward planning. Picture a carefree day off, and you lean toward the moment.
ENTP>ENTJ.plus: You can make ideas happen fast because you can think up fun things and also see them through. When something new is starting, people really count on you.
ENTP>ENTJ.tip: Leave some "no plans" time once a week. If you have separate time to try out ideas, you won't have to break the plans you've made.
ENTP>ENTJ.hidden: On a day the trains stop and your plans fall apart, do you somehow get excited and start looking for another route? That's your temperament's power to enjoy the unplanned. Use it, and people will count on you most when things go wrong.

ENTP>ENTP.title: You're always looking for something interesting.
ENTP>ENTP.body: Is "What if we just stopped doing all of that?" one of your catchphrases? Building ideas by talking with people and flipping the obvious around are exactly the same in your temperament and personality. Your eyes light up at questions with no right answer. In places full of routine tasks, you lose energy easily.
ENTP>ENTP.say: "Who decided it had to be this way, anyway?"
ENTP>ENTP.do: When a new shop opens, you go right away and tell friends how it's different from the others.
ENTP>ENTP.worry: You're good at starting, but you tend to blame yourself for getting bored with keeping things up. Not having energy in a dull place might not be your fault; the place may just not suit you.
ENTP>ENTP.karai: Once a debate heats up, you forget you started on the other side.
ENTP>ENTP.aru: Every time you find a new hobby, you buy all the gear, and three months later you're talking about the next one.
ENTP>ENTP.why: Both your temperament and personality lean toward getting energy from talking, trusting ideas, thinking with logic, and going with the moment. All four match, so your knack for finding new things is very strong. You lose energy with routine work because that knack is so strong.
ENTP>ENTP.yure: Your results tend to stay steady, with the same type coming up again and again. If a different one appears, you may be in a stretch of adapting to a strict role, or low on energy from too little new stimulation.
ENTP>ENTP.plus: Your hobbies change often not because you get bored easily, but because you're quick to find interesting things. All the things you've tried will come in handy in unexpected places.
ENTP>ENTP.tip: For a new hobby, decide on "a one-month trial" before buying gear. If you only buy for the ones that stick, your room and wallet stay neat.
ENTP>ENTP.hidden: You act on ideas, and you also have the power to keep at one thing steadily. It shows when you make a favorite dish again and again, slowly making it your own. Use it, and "fun person" gets "someone you can count on" added to it.

ENTP>INFJ.title: When you listen, you pick up on what people really feel.
ENTP>INFJ.body: When you listen to a friend's worries, you start to see feelings they haven't noticed themselves. Thinking about things that don't exist yet and what's ahead is the same in your temperament and personality. You're both sharp and kind.
ENTP>INFJ.do: You watch favorite movies many times, finding a new way to see them each time.
ENTP>INFJ.worry: Even when you think of something interesting, you hesitate to say it in case it hurts someone. You take in people's feelings so fully that you need plenty of time alone to rest.
ENTP>INFJ.karai: Just talking about a trip, you're already imagining daily life in a town you've never been to.
ENTP>INFJ.aru: While listening to a friend's worries, you said, "Isn't this what you really want?" and they said, "How did you know?"
ENTP>INFJ.why: Trusting ideas is the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament builds ideas by talking, thinks with logic, and acts on the spot. Your personality grew toward thinking alone, sensing feelings, and planning ahead. You can read people's hearts because you're both sharp and kind.
ENTP>INFJ.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Picture yourself chatting loudly with friends, or quietly helping a friend with a problem, and you may get totally different types.
ENTP>INFJ.plus: You notice people's true feelings because you really listen. Someone who notices feelings that are hard to put into words is precious to the people around them.
ENTP>INFJ.tip: On days you help someone with a problem, take a little time for yourself, like buying your favorite drink on the way home. If you rest up, you'll be glad to listen next time too.
ENTP>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to brighten a room by talking. It shows when, at a get-together after a long time, you find yourself joking and keeping things going. Use it, and you'll have more friends you can talk deeply with.

ENTP>INFP.title: You love to daydream, and you're kind.
ENTP>INFP.body: On nights after getting lost in conversation with everyone, you're at home letting your imagination run. Trusting ideas and going with the moment are the same in your temperament and personality. Even when you think up something fun, you're wondering, "Would someone like this?"
ENTP>INFP.do: You and a friend trade silly ideas and get carried away with made-up stories until midnight.
ENTP>INFP.worry: Even if logic says yes, you can't move unless your heart agrees. After a fun time, you find yourself alone, wondering if anything you said hurt someone.
ENTP>INFP.karai: At the bookstore, you find a book on a shelf that has nothing to do with what you came for, and that's what you buy.
ENTP>INFP.aru: Lying in bed, you remember a joke you made while everyone was having fun and wonder, "Did that hurt anyone?"
ENTP>INFP.why: Trusting ideas and going with the moment are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament talks with people and thinks with logic. Your personality grew toward imagining alone and valuing feelings. That's why you look back after a fun time.
ENTP>INFP.yure: You tend to waver on "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself having fun with friends or daydreaming alone.
ENTP>INFP.plus: You replay your words because you don't want to hurt people as much as you want to make them laugh. That's why your humor is kind.
ENTP>INFP.tip: If something you said is bugging you, just ask lightly next time: "About the other day, you're not bothered, right?" Most people don't even remember, so you'll spend less time worrying alone at night.
ENTP>INFP.hidden: Watching a drama, do you ever notice, "Wait, this part doesn't make sense"? That's your temperament's power to quickly spot things that don't add up. Use it at work, and you'll be someone who finds problems early.

ENTP>ENFJ.title: You figure out a way everyone will want to do it.
ENTP>ENFJ.body: You can pitch new projects in a fun way. When someone seems about to be left behind, you notice right away and talk to them. Getting energy from people and getting excited about what's ahead are the same in your temperament and personality.
ENTP>ENFJ.say: "Want to figure out together how to make everyone excited about it?"
ENTP>ENFJ.do: When planning an outing, you quietly pick a place where even the friend who isn't sporty can have fun.
ENTP>ENFJ.worry: Even when you want to say something sharp, you sometimes hold back, thinking about the mood and people's feelings. The more you organize, the less time you have to freely try your ideas.
ENTP>ENFJ.karai: It was just a chat, but now you're pulling everyone in: "Wouldn't it be fun to actually do this?"
ENTP>ENFJ.aru: When you think of something fun, before telling everyone, you go talk one by one to the people who might say no.
ENTP>ENFJ.why: Getting energy from people and trusting ideas are the same in your temperament and personality. Your temperament thinks with logic and acts on the spot. Your personality grew toward caring about feelings and preparing ahead. That's why you can come up with ideas and also check in with people beforehand.
ENTP>ENFJ.yure: You tend to waver on "logic or feelings" and "plan or the moment." The result depends on whether you picture yourself tossing out ideas or bringing everyone together.
ENTP>ENFJ.plus: You go talk to people first because you don't want to leave anyone behind. Not many people can liven things up and look out for everyone too.
ENTP>ENFJ.tip: On days you're the organizer, decide one part of your idea you want to keep before you start. You won't end up giving everything away, so you won't feel uneasy afterward.
ENTP>ENFJ.hidden: Have you ever had a prepared story fall flat, then saved the moment with something else on the spot? That's your temperament's power to change the flow with a quick idea. Trust it too, and you can enjoy days that don't go as planned.

ENTP>ENFP.title: You think things are more fun when everyone does them together.
ENTP>ENFP.body: When you talk, people somehow gather around. Getting energy from people, trusting ideas, and moving lightly are the same in your temperament and personality. While enjoying the conversation, you make sure no one gets left out.
ENTP>ENFP.say: "Love it! Let's all try it next time!"
ENTP>ENFP.do: At family gatherings, you tweak the card game rules so even the little kids can win.
ENTP>ENFP.worry: Even when you want to say clearly what you think is right, you picture their disappointed face and stop. Your interests keep moving, and you also want to make time for people, so there's never enough time.
ENTP>ENFP.karai: Five minutes after saying, "Let's think calmly," you're the most excited one.
ENTP>ENFP.aru: You start to say, "Isn't that a little off?" to a friend, then see their face and add, "But I get how you feel."
ENTP>ENFP.why: Getting energy from people, trusting ideas, and going with the moment are the same in your temperament and personality. The only difference is how you decide. Your temperament thinks with logic, and your personality grew a wish to make people smile. That's why "that's off" and "I get it" come out at the same time.
ENTP>ENFP.yure: The question to watch is "Logic or feelings?" Picture yourself enjoying a debate, and you lean toward logic. Picture yourself cheering up a friend, and you lean toward feelings.
ENTP>ENFP.plus: You soften your words because you care more about the relationship than about being right. People like that naturally end up with more friends they can be honest with.
ENTP>ENFP.tip: When you give your opinion, try saying "I get how you feel" first, then "and also..." What you say stays the same, but it lands differently.
ENTP>ENFP.hidden: Before a big purchase, do you compare reviews and prices across several sites? That's your temperament's power to calmly compare and choose. Use it at work, and you'll go from the fun one to someone people trust with decisions.

ENTP>ISTJ.title: You turn fresh ideas into reality through careful steps.
ENTP>ISTJ.body: Even with a new idea, you start by testing it small and checking the results in numbers. Thinking and judging with logic doesn't waver in any setting. You can widen ideas by talking or progress steadily alone, look at possibilities or check the facts, stay flexible or follow the plan. Your strength is never letting an idea stay just talk.
ENTP>ISTJ.say: "Sounds interesting. But let me check how we did it before."
ENTP>ISTJ.do: When an appliance breaks, you look into the cause yourself before sending it for repair.
ENTP>ISTJ.worry: You want to try new things and also keep the reliable method, so it's hard to decide. When you're stuck enforcing rules for too long, the lack of room for ideas leaves you restless.
ENTP>ISTJ.karai: When a friend asks "How does this outfit look?", you honestly list what works and what doesn't.
ENTP>ISTJ.aru: Even when you think of a new approach, you can't bring it up until you've searched online for every review and example of people who've tried it.
ENTP>ISTJ.why: Thinking things through logically to decide is the same in your temperament and character. That's the part that never wavers. On top of that, an inborn temperament that spreads possibilities by talking and moves lightly overlaps with a learned character that checks facts alone and steadily follows plans. You can back up an idea with data before sharing it because you have both.
ENTP>ISTJ.yure: With three tendencies different, your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself double-checking the usual steps at work, or tossing out ideas in a chat with friends, and you may get a nearly opposite type.
ENTP>ISTJ.plus: Holding back from pitching right away is a sign you want your ideas to be truly useful. A bold idea that's been carefully tested gets approved more easily and lasts longer.
ENTP>ISTJ.tip: Give yourself three days to research, and on day four, talk it over with someone. Getting another person's view gets you to the answer faster than researching alone forever.
ENTP>ISTJ.hidden: During a casual chat on a break, do ideas suddenly start pouring out? That's your born ability to expand your thinking by talking with people. Between your steady solo work, make a little more time to talk, and fresh ideas will find their way into even routine tasks.

ENTP>ISFJ.title: Behind "the usual way," you're already thinking of a better one.
ENTP>ISFJ.body: You finish the task you were given, and somehow there's now a system that makes it easy for anyone next time. You have the kindness to look after people and do what's expected with care, and the curiosity to question the obvious and dream up new ways. Comfort and inspiration, quiet support and lively ideas: that mix makes any place a little better.
ENTP>ISFJ.say: "I'll do the dishes. You sit down."
ENTP>ISFJ.do: You quietly rearrange the shelf your family kept struggling with, without saying a word.
ENTP>ISFJ.worry: You're good at going along with others, but when the same thing repeats, part of you gets bored. Even with a good idea, you sometimes hold it back because of the mood in the room.
ENTP>ISFJ.karai: "Just one more video," you tell yourself, and an hour is gone.
ENTP>ISFJ.aru: You tell your family "The usual way is fine," while in your head you're already thinking up three ways to make the chores easier.
ENTP>ISFJ.why: All four directions differ in this combination. Your inborn temperament loves talking with people, questioning the usual, and trying new things. On top of that, you grew a character that quietly supports others and carefully handles set routines. That's why ideas for improvement keep flowing even though you're modest.
ENTP>ISFJ.yure: With all four tendencies different, your result can change a lot. Picture yourself supporting people at home or work, or following your curiosity to try something new, and your type can flip completely.
ENTP>ISFJ.plus: The improvements you haven't voiced come from watching the people around you so closely. Someone who keeps things feeling safe while making them a little better is valued wherever they go.
ENTP>ISFJ.tip: Instead of "let's change everything," narrow it down to one: "Want to try just this part?" The smaller the suggestion, the more easily it gets accepted.
ENTP>ISFJ.hidden: When two friends argue, have you ever neatly sorted out both sides and said "So this is where you two don't line up"? That's your born ability to organize things with logic. Use it, and you'll become the person everyone turns to for advice.

ENTP>ESTJ.title: A leader who keeps wild ideas running on the ground.
ENTP>ESTJ.body: You change the usual meeting with "Let's do this one standing," and still end it right on time. Getting energy from people and deciding with logic never changes. You can chase new ideas or rely on experience and facts, move flexibly or work to a plan. You have both ideas and the power to carry them out.
ENTP>ESTJ.say: "Want to try doing it differently? I think it'd be faster."
ENTP>ESTJ.do: You suggest a new event for the neighborhood festival, then go on to decide who does what and when on the day.
ENTP>ESTJ.worry: Because you understand why rules matter, balancing them with the urge to try new things is hard. As the leader, you put being right first, and your words can come out harsh.
ENTP>ESTJ.karai: When no one speaks up in a meeting, you're the one who says, "Okay, I'll go first."
ENTP>ESTJ.aru: You bring a brand-new format to the regular meeting on a whim and surprise everyone, yet still wrap it up right on time.
ENTP>ESTJ.why: Gaining energy from people and deciding by logic are the same in your temperament and character. That part never wavers. On top of that, an inborn temperament that chases ideas and acts in the moment is joined by a learned character that trusts experience and facts and moves according to plan. You can make wild ideas work on the ground because you have both.
ENTP>ESTJ.yure: Your answers tend to swing on facts versus hunches and plans versus flexibility. Answer as the person in charge on the ground, and you'll likely get a different result than as your spontaneous weekend self.
ENTP>ESTJ.plus: Few people can make a spur-of-the-moment change and still keep it on schedule. Someone who brings both freshness and reliability can truly change a workplace.
ENTP>ESTJ.tip: On days you're leading, ask "What do you think?" once before giving instructions. You stay just as right, and your words come across less sharply.
ENTP>ESTJ.hidden: In the shower or on a walk, does a new way of doing your work suddenly come to mind? That's your born ability to dream up ideas that don't exist yet. Try them out one at a time, and your workplace will become a lot more interesting.

ENTP>ESFJ.title: You make the usual get-togethers more fun with lively ideas.
ENTP>ESFJ.body: You bring a small new twist to every regular get-together, and still track attendance and fees perfectly. Getting more energy the more you're with people stays the same in every scene. You can come up with new possibilities and care for daily life, think with logic and consider feelings, stay light and stay earnest. You shape fun ideas into something everyone enjoys.
ENTP>ESFJ.say: "Wouldn't it be fun if we did this?"
ENTP>ESFJ.do: At work, you're the one saying, "Let's all go out for lunch today."
ENTP>ESFJ.worry: Even when a cheeky comeback pops into your head, you swallow it for the other person's sake. You love doing things for others, so there's little time left to test your own ideas.
ENTP>ESFJ.karai: After a few days off alone, you start itching to talk to someone.
ENTP>ESFJ.aru: You're the one who suggested the silliest game at the get-together—and also the one who stays to the end, cleaning up most carefully.
ENTP>ESFJ.why: Gaining energy from being with people is exactly the same in your temperament and character. That's your core. On top of that, you have an inborn temperament that dreams up new possibilities, thinks logically, and acts in the moment, and a learned character that cherishes everyday life and people's feelings and organizes things properly. That's why you can goof around and still take such good care of everyone.
ENTP>ESFJ.yure: Three of your four tendencies differ, so your result can change a lot. Answer as the host running the get-together, or as yourself starting a game on a whim, and you might get a different type.
ENTP>ESFJ.plus: People notice how much you do for everyone. Those who can bring fun and a sense of safety together always have people gathering around them.
ENTP>ESFJ.tip: Ask someone to take on at least one part of the cleanup. With your hands freed up, you can enjoy dreaming up the next game even more.
ENTP>ESFJ.hidden: The moment you hear a game's rules, do you instantly see the winning strategy? That's your born ability to build things with logic. Use it while still caring about everyone's feelings, and you'll make proposals at work that really hold together.

ENTP>ISTP.title: Logic and agility get you out of almost any problem.
ENTP>ISTP.body: When you buy a new appliance, you try every button before reading the manual. Thinking with logic and adapting to the situation is you from every angle. You can widen ideas by talking or work quietly alone, see future possibilities or grab the facts in front of you, so people count on you with words and hands alike when things go wrong.
ENTP>ISTP.say: "The manual can wait. Let's turn it on first."
ENTP>ISTP.do: When the train stops on a trip, you quickly find another route and get moving.
ENTP>ISTP.worry: The gap between wanting to debate and wanting to work in silence is big, so people may see you as moody. You also waver between widening ideas and sticking only to what's certain right now.
ENTP>ISTP.karai: When a friend asks how to use something, you skip the explanation and just do it for them.
ENTP>ISTP.aru: Visiting a friend's place, a sticky drawer catches your eye, and while they're talking, you reach over and fix it.
ENTP>ISTP.why: Thinking logically and adapting to the moment are the same in your temperament and character. That part never wavers. On top of that, an inborn temperament that spreads ideas by talking overlaps with a learned character that works with its hands on whatever's in front of it, alone. Your mind and your hands are both fast because you have both.
ENTP>ISTP.yure: Your answers tend to swing on whether people energize you and whether you trust facts or hunches. Picture yourself talking ideas with friends, or fixing something alone, and your result can change.
ENTP>ISTP.plus: Your hands keep working while you listen because you're quick at both thinking and doing. Getting through most problems that smoothly is a real talent.
ENTP>ISTP.tip: When you fix something for someone, just mention "This part was loose." The other person feels reassured, and your skill comes through too.
ENTP>ISTP.hidden: Browsing in a store, do you ever think "Something like this would sell"? That's your born ability to imagine things that don't exist yet. Share those ideas with someone, and they might just spark a new opportunity.

ENTP>ISFP.title: You enjoy things with your mind and with all five senses.
ENTP>ISFP.body: An idea from chatting with friends turns into a handmade trinket once you're home alone. Moving flexibly with the flow and wanting to stay free hasn't changed a bit. You can get lively with people or rest quietly, picture possibilities or savor the senses, think with your head or follow your heart. All of these are your way of enjoying life.
ENTP>ISFP.say: "I want to look at this view a little longer."
ENTP>ISFP.do: An old sign you spot on a walk catches your eye, and before you know it you're photographing it from every angle.
ENTP>ISFP.worry: Even when you want to say something sharp, thinking of the other person makes you hesitate. You love a lively time, but without time alone you wear out fast.
ENTP>ISFP.karai: You keep your calendar open on principle, yet you've already checked every exhibit you care about.
ENTP>ISFP.aru: On a day off with no plans, you wander into a little shop, fall for it, and by the time you leave, you're already planning your next visit.
ENTP>ISFP.why: Adapting to the moment is the one thing that's exactly the same in your temperament and character. That's the part that never wavers. On top of that, an inborn temperament that talks with people and enjoys ideas with logic overlaps with a learned character that savors scenery and sensations alone and values feelings. That's why you enjoy things with your head and also with all your senses.
ENTP>ISFP.yure: With as many as three tendencies different, your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself caught up in debate with friends, or quietly taking in the view alone, and you may get a completely different type.
ENTP>ISFP.plus: Getting absorbed in the fun things around you means you notice interesting things sooner than most. That knack makes your days a little richer than most people's.
ENTP>ISFP.tip: When you find a place you love, bring one friend there next time. Sharing what you like with someone doubles the fun and gives you more to talk about.
ENTP>ISFP.hidden: When the talk turns to something you love, do you find yourself passionately explaining it with your hands flying? That's your born ability to excite people with words. Use it, and the things you love will truly reach the people around you.

ENTP>ESTP.title: When an idea hits, you're on the move right away.
ENTP>ESTP.body: The same week you say "This could be a business," you're already out visiting shops to see it for real. Getting energy from people, thinking with logic, and moving with the flow has always been the same. The difference is how you see: you can imagine what doesn't exist yet and grab the reality in front of you fast. You're quick to think and quick to act.
ENTP>ESTP.say: "Okay, let's go check it out right now!"
ENTP>ESTP.do: When the checkout line is long, you spot a shorter one and switch over in a flash.
ENTP>ESTP.worry: You want both future possibilities and today's fun, so your schedule is always packed. Thinking on the move, you head to the next thing before looking back, and repeat the same mistakes.
ENTP>ESTP.karai: After dinner, before anyone asks "What next?", you're already walking to the second spot.
ENTP>ESTP.aru: The moment you think "I want to go there," you've texted a friend, and by that weekend the two of you are already standing in line out front.
ENTP>ESTP.why: Gaining energy from people, thinking logically, and adapting on the spot are the same in your temperament and character. That part never wavers. Only how you see things differs: an inborn temperament that looks toward ideas and possibilities, plus a strength for trusting what's right in front of you that grew with experience. You can act the moment an idea hits because you see with both eyes.
ENTP>ESTP.yure: Facts or hunches: this is where your answers tend to wobble. Thinking up a new plan, you lean toward hunches; moving around on the ground, you lean toward facts. You can easily move between two types.
ENTP>ESTP.plus: You move fast because you have the drive to never let a chance slip by. Experience has taught you that going to see is quicker than thinking it over.
ENTP>ESTP.tip: For big purchases or important answers, sleep on it before deciding. If you still want it the next morning, it's not just momentum. You really mean it.
ENTP>ESTP.hidden: Hearing about something totally unrelated, do you ever realize "That works the same way as that other thing"? That's your born ability to find hidden connections. Use it at work, and you'll come up with solutions no one else thinks of.

ENTP>ESFP.title: Amazing ideas that make the whole moment fun.
ENTP>ESFP.body: When rain cancels the plan, you turn it into a game night at home on the spot. Getting energy from people and moving lightly with the flow is a strength that never changes. You can dream up new possibilities and savor the fun in front of you, think with logic and sense feelings, so everyone around you ends up smiling too.
ENTP>ESFP.say: "I've got a great idea! Let's do it right now!"
ENTP>ESFP.do: Even on a free day with no plans, you text a friend "What are you up to?" and before long you're out together.
ENTP>ESFP.worry: You want to keep the good vibes, but when you spot a contradiction you can't help calling it out. You're sensitive to feelings, so the moment a room goes cold stays with you for a long time.
ENTP>ESFP.karai: The one who said "let's play just a little" is the one having the most fun at the end.
ENTP>ESFP.aru: You suggest a game that pops into your head at a party, it's a huge hit, and soon you're having the most fun of anyone while running the whole show.
ENTP>ESFP.why: Gaining energy from people and adapting to the moment are the same in your temperament and character. That part never wavers. On top of that, an inborn temperament that has fun with ideas through logic overlaps with a learned character that values the joy in front of it and how everyone feels. That's why you become the center of the circle wherever you go.
ENTP>ESFP.yure: Your swing points are facts or hunches, and logic or feelings. Answer as yourself working on an idea, or playing all-out with friends, and your result can change.
ENTP>ESFP.plus: Seeing you enjoy yourself so fully gives the people around you permission to have fun too. Brightening the mood of a room is a real strength.
ENTP>ESFP.tip: When a game is a hit, set "So when's the next one?" right there. Making plans while everyone's still having fun gets more people on board, and the next time happens naturally.
ENTP>ESFP.hidden: When a friend shares a plan, do you immediately notice "You won't have enough time for that"? That's your born ability to think through the steps in order. Use it alongside your love of fun, and people will see you as not just fun but dependable.
